roles.title: Data / persistence engineer
roles.charter: The Postgres audit ledger: chain integrity, migrations, export, pagination.
roles.trigger: Ledger, migration or export code changes.
roles.produced: docs/LEDGER_TRUNCATION_FINDING.md. This role was queued on a claim that turned out to be FALSE — "the RESTORE path is only described" — when proof:backup-restore has been exercising it on real Postgres in CI all along (16/16 live, including a flipped byte, a truncated archive and a missing manifest all REFUSED). The real gap was next to it: a hash chain detects EDITS, not deletions of its own tail. 40 records seeded on a live Postgres, the last 10 deleted with a plain DELETE, and db:verify-ledger printed "Chain intact" and exited 0. Pinned as an explicit assertion in proof:audit-ledger-pg (14/14), named in the threat model as its own Tampering row, documented in BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md, and answered operationally with db:verify-ledger --min-records N — because the command already REFUSED a missing DATABASE_URL on the grounds that a verifier which green-lights the void is worse than none, and then exited 0 on an empty table.
roles.nextAction: Append-only at the DATABASE grant level: the application role holds DELETE on audit_ledger, and nothing needs it. Revoking it turns the truncation finding from a detection problem into a permissions one. Check what the migration grants and whether the prod compose role is separable.

roles.title: API contract architect
roles.charter: /v1 contract: OpenAPI fidelity, envelope shape, idempotency, versioning and deprecation.
roles.trigger: A route is added or an existing contract changes.
roles.produced: docs/API_CONTRACT_AUDIT.md — the published contract asserted "every route is tenant-scoped: the tenant is derived from the authenticated bearer token", which is the inverse of what 21 of its own 55 operations do (/cp/v1/* carries no principal and is scoped only by a client-supplied ?tenant=); nothing said the whole /cp/v1 surface and GET /v1/keys are registered only under the review-demo profile and 404 elsewhere; three served routes (self-audit, reliability, iac) had drifted out of the spec, the Postman collection and the launch profile at once. The cause was that proof:api-contract read one route file and compared only /v1 while printing "Contract holds" — widened to the whole served surface, plus a zero-routes-parsed guard, self-test 7/7. Also fixed scripts/safety-check.mjs reporting Postman drift with an EMPTY reason.
roles.nextAction: Status codes and response shapes — the deeper half. Nothing compares documented 400/403/404/429 against the handlers that declare them, and test:api is not driven from the spec, so a documented status nobody implemented passes both.

roles.title: DevEx / tooling engineer
roles.charter: The gate fabric itself — preflight, the proof harness, mutation guard, parity checks. Guards the guards.
roles.trigger: A gate is added or changed, or a gate is suspected of passing vacuously. Standing question: is any gate path-filtered away from part of its own subject?
roles.produced: Audited whether any preflight gate is referenced only by a workflow that does not gate every PR — the weakness check-preflight-ci-parity.mjs admits in its own header. Found and fixed one real hole: check-assist-conformance.mjs discovers TWO Assist clients (native/android/core Kotlin, native/desktop/core Rust) but ran only in desktop.yml, filtered to native/desktop/** and native/shared/**, so a change to the KOTLIN client never triggered the gate that binds it — the exact failure it exists to catch, in the client where it had already caught two real defects. Now runs in review-hub-ci.yml on every PR. Two other candidates were the false positive the parity gate already documents (npm alias vs script path), and check-ios-port-sources is correctly scoped since its subject lives entirely inside its filter

roles.title: Identity & Access domain lead
roles.charter: Entra, Okta, Keycloak, Ping, FIDO2. Owns 15 identity dimensions.
roles.trigger: An identity dimension changes, or its wire truth is unverified.
roles.produced: docs/IDENTITY_LIVE_SHAPE_CHECK.md — driven against a live Keycloak 26.4. Three fields sso-session names are NOT wire facts: amr is absent from the access token, the ID token, /userinfo and RFC 7662 introspection alike, leaving only an opaque deployment-configured acr, so single_factor/mfa/phishing_resistant is not derivable from a default IdP; auth_time is absent everywhere, so iat (token issuance) is not when the human authenticated — the same defect class as the RADIUS lastAuthAt finding; and the access token exp is 60s against a 36000s session max, demonstrated live at 75s with the token dead and four SSO sessions still alive. The session record carries no device field at all (id, username, userId, ipAddress, start, lastAccess, rememberMe, clients, transientUser), and two logins by the same user from the same host produced two indistinguishable sessions — precisely the leftover-session case the dimension exists for, so the device-session join must come from the device side. The code is already right (the connector normalizes a bridge-supplied value through oneOf with an unknown fallback and evaluate.ts raises the bar on every unknown); what was missing was the wire-truth record. proof:live-keycloak 14/14.
roles.nextAction: Ten of fifteen dimensions remain unverified against any live IdP, and only Keycloak was driven — Entra DOES emit amr and Okta exposes richer session APIs, so the wire-truth table is one IdP wide. Next: script the Keycloak client setup (KEYCLOAK_LIVE_INTEGRATION.md describes it in prose only, and following that prose cost this shift a 13/14 on a misread mapper value), then take passkey-assurance and token-binding against the same lab.

Those two facts have never been reconciled in writing. Draft the gap analysis: what a hospital's standard paperwork asks for, what SignalGrid can honestly answer today, and which answers need a human lawyer. NEVER signs anything — a signature is one of the owner's five reserved actions.

roles.nextAction: The metric is DEFINED in the sweep: cost-per-shift = monthly agent spend / ledger rows closed, with denominators computable today from committed artifacts (377 Claude-authored commits since 2026-07-20, sim-results durations). Next: publish the denominators now so one owner billing number later yields the ratio instantly. Never publish an invented dollar.
